cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. "This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD." (Jonah 3:3) Last time he went the other way (Jonah 1:3). This time he got up and went. Same Jonah, different direction.
The answer is three-day, friends. Nineveh was "…an exceedingly great city, requiring a three-day journey." (Jonah 3:3) Three DAYS. I get tired just crossing my bakery with a full tray of dough.

The Ninevites believe God, friends. "And the Ninevites believed God." (Jonah 3:5) Jonah's message was "Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!" (Jonah 3:4) And they took it seriously. I think that's a wonderful thing to see.

Everyone joins in, from greatest to least, friends. They did it "…from the greatest of them to the least." (Jonah 3:5) I picture the biggest names and the smallest ones all in the same sackcloth, and I bet nobody was fashion-checking anybody. That's a whole city doing it together.

The king sits in ashes, friends. He "…took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes." (Jonah 3:6) The man had a throne and he traded it for a seat in the ashes. I think that tells you how seriously he took the message.

The answer is True, friends. The decree says, "Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all. They must not eat or drink." (Jonah 3:7) Even the animals are in on this one. Somebody had to tell the herds.

The king says each one should turn from their evil ways and violence, friends. He says, "Let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence in his hands." (Jonah 3:8) The sackcloth and the fasting go with a real turn away from those things.

The answer is False, friends. The king says, "Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish." (Jonah 3:9) I think that's a man hoping, not a man claiming to know. "May" is the whole story there.

God relents from the disaster, friends. "When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them." (Jonah 3:10) Back in verse 9 the king said, "Who knows? God may turn and relent…" (Jonah 3:9) Now we see God relent. I think that's good news for a whole city.
